problem: DRL mapless navigation policies (e.g., Tai et al. 2017) use only undirected exploration: epsilon-greedy or state-independent policy-entropy maximization. This is likely insufficient in environments with long corridors and dead corners, where agents fall into local minima and converge to sub-optimal policies.
motivation: Mapless navigation removes the need for SLAM and a prior map, requiring only a relative goal pose from cheap localization such as Wi-Fi or visible light. Prior DRL navigation work was tested in environments that posed little exploration challenge. Pathak et al.'s Intrinsic Curiosity Module showed that self-supervised prediction error can drive agents toward novel states, which suggests it could help navigation in structurally harder maps.
key_idea: Add ICM curiosity (forward-model prediction error on learned laser features) as an intrinsic reward to a shaped extrinsic navigation reward in A3C, so that exploration is state-dependent and the agent escapes local minima.
insight: Curiosity-based, state-dependent exploration beats state-independent entropy regularization, and the two combine best. Without LSTM on Map1, success rises from 34.3% (Entropy) to 65.7% (ICM) to 73.3% (ICM+Entropy). With LSTM it rises from 96.7% to 98.7% to 100%, and mean steps fall from 102.2 to 75.2. The gains grow on harder unseen maps: on Map4, Entropy reaches 34.3% SR and ICM+Entropy 55.0%. On the structurally different but easy Map2, ICM alone is best. The authors attribute ICM agents' shorter paths to seeing more of the environment rather than re-exploring the same areas. The LSTM is essential: without it no configuration converges to a good policy.
method: Mapless nav MDP: the state is a 72-dim 2D laser scan (max range 7 m) plus the relative goal (distance, sin and cos of bearing); there are 3 discrete actions.

Shaped extrinsic reward: +1 at goal, -5 on collision, and otherwise λ^g × the decrease in goal distance. Added to this are a -0.05 penalty for zero displacement and a heading-to-goal orientation term scaled by 1/(200π).

ICM: an MLP feature encoder φ (128-64-16, ELU) over consecutive laser scans. An inverse model predicts a_t from (φ_t, φ_{t+1}) with cross-entropy loss. A forward model predicts φ_{t+1} from (φ_t, one-hot a_t) with MSE loss. The losses are weighted (1-λ^f) for inverse and λ^f=0.2 for forward, to avoid trivial constant features.
Intrinsic reward R^i = ½‖φ̂_{t+1} − φ_{t+1}‖², combined as R = R^e + λ^i R^i with λ^i = 1.

A3C actor-critic: 2 conv layers (8 filters, stride 2, kernels 5 and 3), then FC 64-16 as the laser embedding. This is concatenated with the goal and fed to a 16-cell LSTM, whose output is concatenated with the goal again to produce softmax policy and value heads. Optional entropy regularization uses β=0.01.
Training: 22 asynchronous threads with shared Adam (lr 1e-4), rollout K=50, γ=0.99, 3M iterations (~15 h on CPU), trained on Map1 only.

setting.backbone: small CNN + LSTM actor-critic with MLP-based ICM (trained from scratch with A3C)
setting.training_data: RL in a single simulated 2D floor plan (Map1, 5.33 m × 3.76 m) with random start/goal pairs; 3M iterations, 22 A3C threads; no extra data
setting.observation: 72-beam 2D laser range scan (max 7 m) + relative goal position (distance, sin/cos of relative orientation)
setting.action_space: discrete: go straight 0.06 m / turn left 8° / turn right 8°
setting.privileged: relative goal pose provided at every step (assumed obtainable via cheap localization); no map

numbers_note: Custom 2D maps rather than a standard benchmark. 'split' is mapped as follows: Map1, the training map, is 'val-seen'; Map2-4, unseen maps, are 'test-unseen'. Training curves (average reward/steps, mean and CI over 3 runs) appear only in Fig. 4 with no numbers. Tables report one evaluation per configuration; the paper does not say which run. w/o-LSTM ICM (65.7% SR) is omitted from the entries.
results: On the training map, A3C+ICM+Entropy with LSTM reaches 100% success with 75.16 mean steps, versus 96.7% and 102.22 steps for entropy-only A3C and 88.3% and 173.06 steps for plain A3C. On unseen maps, ICM+Entropy is best on the harder Map3 (72.7% vs 69.7% Entropy) and Map4 (55.0% vs 34.3% Entropy and 44.3% A3C-). On the structurally different but easy Map2, ICM alone is best (87.7% vs 82.7%). Curiosity also consistently shortens paths.
limitations: Evaluated only in a tiny custom 2D laser simulator (5.33 m × 3.76 m maps) with a single training map; there are no real-robot experiments, which the authors list as future work.
Gains are inconsistent: ICM+Entropy is worse than ICM on Map2, and ICM alone is worse than Entropy on Map3. Only 3 training runs; the tables report single evaluations without variance across seeds.
Reward weights (λ^i, λ^f and the shaping terms) are hand-tuned; adaptive weighting is left to future work.
builds_on: Virtual-to-real DRL mapless navigation (Tai et al. 2017)
